\newcommand{\TextRetrieval}{Code-mixing degrades the base paper's English retriever: for Heavy posts only 27.0\% of its top-10 cases are those it retrieves for the English original (56.9\% for Light). LaBSE and multilingual mpnet without fine-tuning help on Light but stay near 31--33\% on Heavy, while the contrastively fine-tuned encoder keeps 53.3\% (Light 73.2\%), the largest gain of all encoders, and the strategy distribution of its retrieved cases is the most stable across languages. The price is a lower problem-type precision than the English encoder (31.5 vs 33.8 on Heavy): the fine-tuned space favours the same cases as the English query over the same problem label.}
\newcommand{\TextQuality}{On Heavy, CodeMixESC reaches ROUGE-L 9.24 and chrF 18.97, above MultiAgentESC (5.66 / 16.97) and above the translate-pivot (8.62 / 19.13); the single-call baselines reach 7.50 (zero-shot) and 5.50 (few-shot CoT). On Light, CodeMixESC reaches ROUGE-L 10.60 and chrF 18.92, on par with MultiAgentESC (10.45 / 18.91) and above the translate-pivot (5.75 / 16.42); the single-call baselines reach 11.58 (zero-shot) and 11.98 (few-shot CoT). On EN, CodeMixESC reaches ROUGE-L 11.04 and chrF 19.65, above MultiAgentESC (10.44 / 19.01); the single-call baselines reach 10.22 (zero-shot) and 10.90 (few-shot CoT). Paired bootstrap over conversations (Table~\ref{tab:significance}): Heavy vs MultiAgentESC: ROUGE-L +3.58 [+1.83, +5.27], $p<0.01$; Light vs MultiAgentESC: ROUGE-L +0.15 [-1.75, +2.09], $p=0.93$; Heavy vs Translate-Pivot: ROUGE-L +0.62 [-1.09, +2.40], $p=0.47$; Light vs Translate-Pivot: ROUGE-L +4.85 [+3.03, +6.79], $p<0.01$.}
\newcommand{\TextRegister}{Register match (lower is better): on Light the mean CMI gap is 0.137 for CodeMixESC, 0.141 for MultiAgentESC, 0.136 for the pivot and 0.148 before the Register Gate; on Heavy the mean CMI gap is 0.120 for CodeMixESC, 0.357 for MultiAgentESC, 0.208 for the pivot and 0.136 before the Register Gate. The gate's own effect on the CMI gap (with minus without): Light -0.012 [-0.022, -0.003], $p<0.01$; Heavy -0.017 [-0.033, -0.001], $p=0.04$.}
\newcommand{\TextStability}{Jensen--Shannon divergence between the strategy distributions on the English and the Hinglish versions of the same turns (lower = less disturbed by code-mixing): CodeMixESC 0.022 (Light) / 0.016 (Heavy); MultiAgentESC 0.014 (Light) / 0.081 (Heavy); Translate-Pivot 0.015 (Light) / 0.016 (Heavy).}
\newcommand{\TextAblation}{On Heavy, CodeMixESC: ROUGE-L 9.24, CMI gap 0.120; w/o Register Gate: ROUGE-L 9.10, CMI gap 0.136; w/o retriever fine-tuning: ROUGE-L 9.25, CMI gap 0.116; w/o cross-lingual retriever: ROUGE-L 10.44, CMI gap 0.099. Each row removes one component from the full system on the same turns, so the differences isolate the retriever fine-tuning, the cross-lingual retriever and the Register Gate.}
\newcommand{\TextJudge}{Pairwise judgement by \texttt{gemma-4-31b-it} in both presentation orders (a win only if both orders agree): CodeMixESC vs MultiAgentESC on Light: overall win/tie/lose 74/6/20 percent of the turns (p < 0.01); CodeMixESC vs Translate-Pivot on Light: overall win/tie/lose 44/24/32 percent of the turns (p = 0.42); CodeMixESC vs MultiAgentESC on Heavy: overall win/tie/lose 86/10/4 percent of the turns (p < 0.01); CodeMixESC vs Translate-Pivot on Heavy: overall win/tie/lose 56/20/24 percent of the turns (p = 0.02).}
\newcommand{\TextEfficiency}{CodeMixESC needs 10.20 LLM calls per turn on Light vs 9.66 for MultiAgentESC and 11.72 for the pivot; 10.70 LLM calls per turn on Heavy vs 10.22 for MultiAgentESC and 11.22 for the pivot: the profiler and the retriever add no LLM call, and the Register Gate at most one.}
\newcommand{\TextCases}{The cases are selected by fixed rules (register rescues, gate rewrites, strategy changes and failures), so they show both what the components fix and where the system still misses the seeker's register.}
\newcommand{\TextAbstract}{On ESConv-HiEn Heavy the fine-tuned retriever keeps 53\% of the cases retrieved for the English original, against 27\% for the base paper's encoder, and CodeMixESC's replies reach ROUGE-L 9.24 against 5.66 for MultiAgentESC with a smaller register gap and at most one extra LLM call per turn.}
\newcommand{\TextConclusion}{CodeMixESC adapts a multi-agent emotional-support pipeline to code-mixed Hinglish help-seekers without fine-tuning the agents. A contrastively fine-tuned multilingual encoder makes retrieval robust to code-mixing (27\% $\rightarrow$ 53\% Overlap@10 on Heavy), the register profile and the Register Gate bring the replies closer to the seeker's language mix at a cost of at most one LLM call, and ESConv-HiEn makes the effect of code-mixing measurable on parallel conversations. Future work: spontaneous (not rewritten) Hinglish, other Indian languages and human evaluation with native speakers.}
